Class DefaultContext

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.inject.context.DefaultContext
All Implemented Interfaces:
Context
public final class DefaultContext extends Object implements Context
Default Context: loads all Factory and Scope services, wraps each factory provider with a cycle guard and its declared scope, checks that every live bean's dependencies are bound, and resolves keys lazily. Fallback factories (Factory#isDefault()) bind only keys no other live factory claims. The registry is immutable after construction; resolution is thread-safe.

A scoping annotation with no Scope service is child-local: the ChildContexts that host it cache its instances, and resolving such a bean here fails with a ScopeResolutionException.

new DefaultContext() loads all registered Factory, Scope, and Condition services. The injector that owns this context attaches itself via setInjector(Injector) immediately after construction, which is what lets Key.of(Injector.class) resolve, and builds the eager singletons (Factory#isEager()) still live in the registry.

    • setInjector

      public void setInjector(Injector injector)
      Attaches the Injector this context resolves Key.of(Injector.class) to, resolves the ConstructionListeners, then builds the eager singletons, which the listeners see. Called once by the injector that owns this context, immediately after construction.

      When building a listener or an eager singleton fails, this context is closed, destroying the singletons already built, and the failure is thrown.

      Parameters:
      injector - the owning injector
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if an injector is already attached

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes the live child contexts, newest first, then destroys every tracked scoped instance (invoking each factory's @PreDestroy) in reverse creation order, and rejects further resolution. Failures are collected as suppressed exceptions on the first one thrown, so every child and every instance is still given a chance to close or destroy. Idempotent.
      Specified by:
      close in interface Context
